title: Open WebUI calendar event update -- T1565.001 unchecked destination calendar_id moves events across owners
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-54006 (GHSA-f3g7-59qc-pqg6,
CVSS 4.3 MEDIUM), affecting Open WebUI prior to 0.9.6.

`POST /api/v1/calendars/events/{event_id}/update` correctly validates
that the caller has write access to the calendar the event CURRENTLY
belongs to -- but never validates the DESTINATION `calendar_id`
supplied in the request body. The model layer then persists the new
`calendar_id` unconditionally. A regular user-role account can create
an event in their own calendar (a legitimate action) and then, through
this same update endpoint, move that event into ANY other user's
calendar whose id they know -- bypassing the authorization check that
the sibling `create_event` endpoint correctly performs.

Detection logic flags an event-update request whose `calendar_id`
field differs from the event's CURRENT calendar and whose destination
calendar does not belong to the requesting user -- the exact
authorization gap this advisory describes.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (open-webui, via
GHSA and NVD), fixed in 0.9.6.
